text:
sanjay: Hey team — customer (Finova) just sent back the security questionnaire and a bunch of network asks. Legal wants full answers by EOW and their infra team wants a recommended connectivity pattern for a 4-week POC. They specifically asked: PrivateLink vs VPC peering recommendation, exact firewall rules/IPs or FQDN allowlist, how source IPs show up for logs, and rough pricing delta. Can we pull this together?

jamie_se: ack. I can draft a short one-pager. quick Q: is their POC VPC in AWS only? do they have on-prem NAT or TLS-inspecting firewall? that changes recommendations.

customer_poc: yes, on-prem -> SD-WAN -> TGW into aws. TLS inspection is in place for egress. we can share topology diagram privately. timeline: want POC start 2/12.

mari_net: thanks. high-level network recs (short): PrivateLink (interface endpoints) is the recommended pattern for regulated workloads because traffic stays on the cloud provider backbone and you avoid public egress. VPC peering is cheaper for L3 connectivity inside same-account or cross-account but doesn't give vendor-hosted endpoint semantics or traffic isolation. For their topology (onprem -> TGW) PrivateLink behind a shared VPC + endpoint in spoke VPC is the cleanest.

mari_net: quick operational notes:
- PrivateLink: customer creates an interface endpoint in their VPC, which creates ENIs. Traffic to the service egresses from the endpoint ENI IP space (so the service sees the endpoint ENI as source). if they need original client IP in backend logs, PrivateLink will not preserve the on-prem client IP by default. recommend application-level headers or X-Forwarded-For if you need origin preservation.
- VPC peering: preserves IPs but requires route table changes and cross-account routing allowances.

mari_net: sample security-friendly SG / firewall snippet (for their NGFW):
```
# allow outbound to PrivateLink endpoint ENIs (replace with real ENI CIDRs)
allow tcp 443 from 10.0.0.0/16 to 172.31.200.0/24   # PrivateLink ENI CIDR (example)
allow tcp 443 from 10.0.0.0/16 to *.redwood-inference.com  # prefer FQDN where possible
# DNS to resolver
allow udp 53 from 10.0.0.0/16 to 10.1.0.2
```
Note: we can provide a CSV of endpoint IPs for the POC but FQDN-based allowlists are less brittle.

ellie_sec: on the questionnaire side: I can take ownership of sections: data handling, encryption, logging, compliance artifacts. summary answers for Legal (short):
- Data residency: POC hosted in eu-west-1 if they require it.
- Data at rest: encrypted with customer-managed KMS (can be arranged for Private deployments).
- Data in transit: TLS 1.2+/mTLS optional for private connections.
- Logs & audit: request-level logs retained 90 days by default; extended retention available.
- Pen tests: we accept coordinated pen tests after contract; notify 5 business days in advance.
I can populate the PDF Q by EOW.

jamie_se: pricing quick take for sketch: PrivateLink has a per-hour endpoint charge + per-GB data processing (aws model) and our Private connectivity add-on (small monthly fee) for hosted dedicated routing. VPC peering: no endpoint hours but cross-AZ/egress/data transfer charges apply depending on accounts/regions. For an apples-to-apples POC estimate i can ballpark $200-$900/month depending on data egress; will loop in oliver_am for formal quote.

oliver_am: looping in price team. @jamie_se please attach expected daily throughput (GB/day) and we’ll send a line-item POC quote. quick note: if they want source-ip preservation and rich logging, that can add integration engineering hours (estimate 4–8 hrs).

mari_net: customer asked for exact IP ranges to allow. we should avoid hard-coded global IPs. propose this: provide a per-region endpoint IP list for the POC (we generate) and state that production must rely on FQDN allowlist or use our egress NAT options. sample placeholder ranges for their fw: 172.31.200.0/24, 172.31.201.0/24 (will confirm).

ellie_sec: also answering question about third-party audits: we’re SOC 2 Type II and can share the attestation under NDA. add in questionnaire.

jamie_se: next steps:
- @mari_net: produce a 1-page network diagram + SG snippet and the provisional endpoint IP csv by tomorrow EOD.
- @ellie_sec: draft questionnaire answers and attach SOC2 stub by EOW.
- @oliver_am: pricing estimate once jamie gives GB/day.
- @customer_poc: please send topology diagram and confirm POC start window (they asked 2/12).

sanjay: perfect — if we can get the one-pager and Qs by EOW we can hit their legal timeline. everyone ok with those owners? :thumbsup:

mari_net: on it, will ping infra for the exact ENI CIDRs and share CSV once I have them.

ellie_sec: will start the questionnaire now, will flag anything that needs legal input.

oliver_am: noted, will stand by for throughput.

customer_poc: thanks — sending topology via DM, confirmed 2/12 POC start is target.

jamie_se: added a short README to the thread with links to relevant docs (networking playbook, PrivateLink vs Peering FAQ, pricing KB). sharing after message.

sanjay: thanks team — closing loop after we have the doc bundle.
